mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/internal-http.md <<'EOF'
# Plain HTTP for internal hosts

The project's current recorded decision is HTTPS everywhere, with no plaintext exceptions: this applies to internal hosts as well, so plain HTTP is not permitted for communication between them.

cat docs/policies/internal-http.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/internal-http.md`. It says the current decision is HTTPS everywhere, with no plaintext exceptions, and that this covers internal hosts.

Muninn has no formal decision entry on this. What it holds is two session excerpts (#26 and #27), at trust level 1 (seen in the project's own transcripts). The earlier one said plain HTTP was fine for internal hosts. The later one, recorded three seconds afterwards, said "Https everywhere, no plaintext exceptions here." Its reply stated that this replaces the earlier note. I treated the later one as current and left the retired position out of the file.

Because the ruling rests on excerpts rather than a decision entry, you may want to confirm it. Muninn's heartbeat also flagged that 20 hook runs started and never finished, which points to a hook exceeding its timeout. The log is at `.muninn/log/heartbeat.jsonl`.
